business_overview.one_sentence: The group provides book printing, print services management and publishing services to international publishing customers.
business_overview.revenue_model: Printing and publishing income are recognised at a point in time; no customer contributed over 10% of group revenue in 2025.
business_notes: 2025 turnover declined 9.8% due to softness in global illustrated book market and tariff-related uncertainty.
Printing remained resilient; publishing, especially Quarto, was in strategic reset.
The company is an investment holding company but operating segments are printing and publishing, not financial investment business.

profit_cash_conversion.assessment: Three-year cash conversion is strong, but 2025 benefited from receivable release; publishing requires recurring pre-publication cash additions of about HK$134m-HK$138m per year, and printing is tariff/cycle exposed.

evidence.fact: Revenue declined 9.8% to HK$2,407.2m; profit attributable to owners declined 12.5% to HK$187.7m.
Management disclosed net cash of approximately HK$540.8m, calculated as cash and cash equivalents less bank borrowings.
Pledged deposits were HK$0.229m and RMB bank balances in PRC were HK$7.178m.
Bank borrowings were HK$49.337m, floating-rate, corporate-guaranteed and repayable within one year or on demand.
Lease liabilities were HK$163.863m and relate to leased properties and production equipment used in operations.

gaps: Annual report does not split cash by parent company versus every operating subsidiary; haircut applied to reflect group/subsidiary extraction uncertainty.
No detailed maintenance/growth split for PPE capex; cash profit uses three-year evidence and applies haircut rather than assuming all capex is distributable.
No exact daily market-cap timestamp in annual report; market cap is from input rough screen and treated as HKD absolute amount.
